summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his lecture on the conditions of salah (prayer), specifically focusing on the fourth condition regarding proper covering (awrah) during prayer and in public. He explains the fundamental Islamic principle that worship acts default to prohibition unless explicitly permitted, while customary matters default to permissibility unless prohibited. Sh. Ali Mashhour outlines the eight conditions of hijab for women in public, beginning with the first two: that clothing must cover the entire body except hands and face, and that the garment itself must not be an adornment that draws attention, explaining the Quranic term 'tabarruj' (display) through its etymological connection to 'burj' (tower), illustrating how clothing should not make one stand out like a tower among buildings.
